## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

The *Gotamivatthadānapañha* ("Why Should Gifts Be Given To the Order Rather Than To the Buddha?", Mil 6.1.2) is a section of the *Milindapañha* belonging to the late canonical or paracanonical Pali strata. The text addresses the dilemma regarding the propriety and merit of offering gifts to the monastic community (*saṅgha*) as opposed to the Buddha directly, a discussion intimately linked with the episode of Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī offering a pair of cloths.

 It also shares themes and references with MN 3, SN 2.30, AN 1.170, and Mil 6.4.2, alongside multiple Chinese and Tibetan parallels and discussions, including the Madhyama Āgama (MĀ 180), the *Fenbie bushi jing* (分別布施經, T 84), the *Dazhidulun* (T 1509.22), the *Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā* (T 1545.178), and narrative collections (T 202.52, T 203.50, T 212.14).

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
